title: Research: Security Properties of HL7 Interface Engines in Clinical Deployments
summary: An analysis of HL7 interface engine deployments, noting that message-level authentication is rarely implemented and that integration engines hold unusually broad access across clinical systems.
content:
## Overview

Our research team is publishing the following analysis. An analysis of HL7 interface engine deployments, noting that message-level authentication is rarely implemented and that integration engines hold unusually broad access across clinical systems.

**Scope:** Configuration review study

**Confidence:** Moderate

## Data and methodology

Based on configuration reviews performed during consulting engagements. Deployments reviewed skew toward larger organisations that commission such reviews.

## Findings

- HL7 messaging typically relies on network-level trust rather than message-level authentication, so a foothold on the interface network is sufficient to inject messages.
- Integration engines hold write access to a broader set of clinical systems than almost any other component, which makes them high-value.
- Message content is logged by default in most engines, which is what made this component class disproportionately exposed to logging-library vulnerabilities.
